class_and_unit_proof: Z[phi] is norm-Euclidean, hence has class number one. Its units are +/-phi^n. Since phi has norm -1 and signs (+,-), the narrow and ordinary class groups agree. The totally positive units are exactly phi^(2n), and each is the square of the unit phi^n. Thus a squarefree ideal product has a (+,-) generator unique up to the chosen phi^(2Z) fundamental domain.
coefficient_scope: all squarefree prime-ideal representatives of K-square directions of norm <=128, including the inert dyadic ideal, the ramified prime over 5, inert odd primes, and both choices over every split rational prime
complete_mirror_class_proof: For a primitive r=(x,y), q(r) divides 2(a*x,(y,Lambda)) because the Leech lattice is even unimodular. Away from primes over 2a, local unimodularity and primitivity exclude positive q-valuation. At an odd prime P dividing squarefree (a), positive q-valuation forces y in P*Lambda; then x is a P-unit and q=-a*x^2 mod P^2, so the valuation is exactly one. These odd choices are independent. The prime (2) is inert. If 2 does not divide a, a primitive x gives dyadic valuation zero, while nonunit x and primitive y allow only valuation one. If 2 divides squarefree a, evenness makes q divisible by 2 and q|2I(r) bounds its valuation by one whenever y is primitive; if y is not primitive then x is a unit and q=-a*x^2 mod 4 again has valuation one. Thus the dyadic exponents are {0,1} for 2 not dividing a and {1} for 2 dividing a, with no dyadic spatial gate.
direction_interpretation: the squarefree ideal representatives parameterize K-square coefficient directions; removing a nonunit square changes the integral lattice in general, so this is not an integral-host classification
height_zero_proof: A primitive height-zero mirror would have q=y^2 generating (2): evenness gives (2)|q and q|2(y,Lambda) plus primitive unimodularity gives the reverse valuation bound. After unit rescaling, y^2=2 and Tr(y^2)=4. But writing y=u+phi*v gives Tr(y^2)=u^2+(u+v)^2+2v^2. The Leech minimum is four, so every nonzero y has trace at least eight (if v=0, the first two terms coincide; if v is nonzero, 2v^2 is already at least eight). Therefore there are no height-zero mirrors.
scope: Exact bounded census of squarefree K-square coefficient directions, complete primitive local mirror-norm classes, and first necessary Leech Gram packets. Necessary triples need not be realised Leech pairs or accepted Vinberg roots. Nonunit square multiples can give different integral hosts, and later mirrors can cut every displayed patch. This is not a census of integral hosts and does not prove global nonreflectivity.
